/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:258:For cases where "did the right tools fire" isn't enough — anything graded on the quality
of the final answer — the judge grades the run against your **expected output** if you set one, and against the user prompt otherw
ise. It's advisory: it produces a score and a rationale, but doesn't gate the run unless you ask it to.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:262:* When grading against the prompt rather than an expected output, scores are capped at 0.
85 — you can't get a "perfect" without saying what perfect means.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:303:> If **Run all** is disabled, no models are selected or a run for that suite is already i
n progress. For non-environment suites, a missing connected server also disables it. When every model the suite would run is out o
f MCPJam credits, **Run all** and each case's **Run** button are disabled with an "Out of MCPJam credits · resets in …" tooltip —
switching any case to a model from your own providers re-enables those buttons. The header pickers will tell you which condition a
pplies.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:309:### Pre-run credit estimate
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:311:When enabled on your account, an **ⓘ** icon appears beside run controls before you launch
. Hovering it shows an estimated credit cost for the run about to start — priced against the exact models, cases, and iteration co
unt the button will execute.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:317:* **Run / Run compare** in the template editor — prices the currently selected models and
the current (possibly unsaved) prompt.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:324:| Estimated: \~N credits — based on your recent runs | Full coverage, grounded in your ow
n run history |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:325:| Estimated: \~N credits — partly based on recent runs | Full coverage, partially grounde
d in history |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:326:| Rough estimate: \~N credits — improves after first run | Full coverage, heuristic only
(no history yet) |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:327:| At least \~N credits — part of this run is unpriced | Some models or run slices could n
ot be priced |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:330:1 credit = \$0.01. Your free daily allowance and any BYOK keys change what is actually de
ducted. The estimate is informational only — it never blocks or gates a run.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:445:| **Per-turn timeout** | How long one model turn (prompt → response) may run. |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:451:An empty field shows the platform default it inherits rather than a blank — "no value" me
ans "whatever the platform decides". Clearing a field saves as `null`, which resets to the platform default. The API accepts these
at `settings.executionBudgets.*` on the suite PATCH.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:453:Platform-enforced ceilings apply: a value above the platform ceiling is refused at save t
ime, naming the field and the bound. Organization-level ceilings are enforced by the server.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:457:Each eval suite has a **Default Execution Config** section that controls the model, syste
m prompt, temperature, tool approval, connection settings, capabilities, and host context used when running the suite.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:459:* **Model and prompt** — Set the default model ID, system prompt, and temperature for all
runs in the suite. When running evals against MCP Apps that render widgets, the eval harness automatically enables browser intera
ction (screenshot, click, type) for any model that supports both vision and tool calling — not just Claude. Models that lack visio
n or tool calling run without browser interaction.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:478:The suite-level **system prompt** and **temperature** are runtime defaults: when a test c
ase does not set its own system prompt or temperature, the suite values are used for that iteration. A per-case override always wi
ns — the suite default only fills the gap.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:482:> If you have existing suites where test cases do not specify a system prompt, those case
s will now run with the suite's system prompt applied. Cases that already set their own system prompt are unaffected.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:486:The **CI** tab (when enabled for your project) shows only CI-active suites — suites creat
ed by the SDK or suites that CI has reported into at least once. Playground-only suites stay in the **Evaluate** tab. If a project
has no CI evals yet, the CI tab shows a quickstart prompt.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:557:* **Run insights** — an AI-written diff against your previous completed run: which cases
moved, which tools changed behavior, which models diverged. Skim this first; it usually points at the right rabbit hole. The model
pass is **included with MCPJam and consumes no credits**; it counts against a daily insight quota shared with swarm wave and user
-testing insights. Guests browsing without a signed-in account will see a **Sign in** prompt in the insights band — signing in unl
ocks the feature without losing your place.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:558:* **Overview tab** — every run with its summary metrics, plus a Suite Health chart whose
bars link to individual run rows. Click in for the iteration-level breakdown. The table shows **Date** first, then **Run**, with s
eparate **Client**, **Model**, **Platform**, **Commit**, **Rate**, **Latency**, **Tokens**, and **Calls** columns. The Client colu
mn counts unique clients; when there are more than two, a **+N** badge appears — hover it to see all clients in a tooltip.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:578:* **Stamped.** The platform decides a run's `source` itself, and a caller cannot
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:588:strength of it. Alongside both, the platform records the credential the request
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:595:When two or more host configurations are attached to a suite, a **By case / By host** tog
gle appears. **By host** shows a matrix — one column per host, one row per case. Each cell shows pass/fail dots, pass rate, median
latency, and token usage. A host detached after runs were recorded stays visible, labelled **historical**.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:597:### Cost
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:599:Every iteration carries the MCPJam-billed cost of the model work it did,
